Deși Yunnan ocupă mai puțin de 4% din teritoriul Chinei, aici sălășluiesc peste jumătate dintre păsările și mamiferele din această țară.

programme.title: Odraslele furtunii
programme.desc: În Islanda, doar unul din șase pui a supraviețuit. Abandonat de părinți, acum trebuie să se descurce singur. Turma de reni înoată aproape patru kilometri în ape deschise. În Scoția, 35.000 de foci cenușii sosesc pentru sezonul anual de reproducere.

programme.title: Ciudat, sălbatic și minunat
programme.desc: Traversați Africa pentru a arunca o privire la variatele și neobișnuitele strategii de supraviețuire ale animalelor de aici. Priviți acești magicieni furioși, înaripați și acoperți cu solzi, de la flamingo viu colorați la șopârle care dispar rapid, găsindu-și mâncare, scăpând de prădătorii și găsindu-și parteneri în condițiile cele mai vitrege.

programme.title: Cer sălbatic
programme.desc: Eterna căutare a apei definește viața animalelor sălbatice din Africa. Asistați la cea mai mare frenezie a hranei marine de pe Pământ, vedeți cum își iau cobrele energie solară și urmăriți gnu și elefanții în migrațiile lor epice.

programme.title: Vânătorii Africii
programme.desc: În timp ce masculii dominanți cutreieră teritoriile din apropiere, sarcinile de vânătoare revin celor nouă leoaice puternice din turma Mwamba. Vedeți cum se descurcă acestea cu apropierea sezonului ploios și cu șase adolescenți cu apetit nemărginit.

programme.title: Vânătorii Africii
programme.desc: Leoaicele pornesc să recupereze masculii de care au nevoie pentru a vâna bivoli, dar trebuie să traverseze un râu plin de crocodili. Milo, singurul pui din puternica turmă Mwamba, este salvat de fălcile înțepătoare și cimentează viitorul familiei.

programme.title: Urgențe în sălbăticie
programme.desc: Vară aglomerată la RSPCA Wildlife Hospital, unde veterinarul Emily ajută o koala să elimine gaze. Echipa luptă împotriva unei epidemii de paralizie lorikeet. Veterinarul Karina folosește un ursuleț de pluș pentru a salva un pui de pteropus.

programme.title: Regatele sălbatice ale Europei
programme.desc: Vezi cum cea mai de seamă arhitectură a Europei a creat sanctuare pentru unele din cele mai rare specii. Mergi în Franța, Scoția și Spania, unde foci, păsări, tritoni, pisici sălbatice și șerpi prosperă printre monumente străvechi, la marginea apei.

programme.title: Simțurile animalelor
programme.desc: Undele sonore sunt produse de mișcare. Animalele au fost înzestrate, prin evoluție, cu organe pentru detectarea undelor sonore în aer sau în apă, pentru a percepe mișcarea în mediul ambient. Iată câteva animale cu simț al auzului supra-dezvoltat.

programme.title: Latura sălbatică a Lunii
programme.desc: Vezi cum fazele lunii stabilesc ritmul unei lupte nesfârșite între prădător și pradă. Plutește alături de colugo, savurează un festin cu fructe de mare alături de macaci și vezi o haită de lei care încearcă să transforme în cină un pui de elefant.

programme.title: Apele Arabiei
programme.desc: Recifele colorate ale Arabiei sunt reședința unora dintrei cei mai impresionanți iluzioniști din natură. Aceste creaturi pot pulsa colorat, se pot transforma într-o clipită sau pot da dovadă de abilități uluitoare de expert, fiindcă în aceste ape deghizarea este esențială.

programme.title: Apele Arabiei
programme.desc: În largul coastei Omanului, clima de vară aduce nutrimenți din adâncurile oceanului, unde se întâlnesc cu soarele Arabiei, generând o explozie de vitalitate. Peștișorii depun icre, umplând apele cu ouă. Astfel se creează un bufet care tentează prădătoarele.

programme.title: Urgențe în sălbăticie
programme.desc: Veterinarii Emily și Martine sterilizează o koala, dar operația se complică. O echidnă rătăcită primește ajutor de la veterinarul Nigel, agentul de salvare Chantelle ajută o șopârlă și veterinarul Karina investighează un posibil furt de păsări.

programme.title: Misterele fluviului Mekong
programme.desc: Munți abrupți și musoni tropicali definesc valea fluviului Mekong pe traseul său prin Laos. Surprinde imagini cu animalele sălbatice care își găsesc refugiul în ecosistemele sale vibrante, de la macaci la pescăruși și giboni cu creastă neagră.

programme.title: Abisul extraterestru
programme.desc: Faceți cunoștință cu multe ciudățenii din ocean și aflați cum miliarde de ani de schimbări, de la epoci de gheață la asteroizi, le-au schimbat aspectul și abilitățile. Vedeți viermi orbi care pescuiesc, rechini cu picioare, crabi care urcă în copaci și multe altele.

programme.title: Priveliști nedescoperite
programme.desc: Costa Rica este un univers în sine - un coridor tropical aflat între două oceane mari, cu râuri furioase și vulcani care stau să răbufnească. Atunci când vulcanii săi erup, depozitează minerale în sol, fertilizând regiunea și creând biodiversitatea amplă din această țară.

programme.title: Anotimpurile sălbăticiei în America
programme.desc: E primăvară: anotimpul curtării și al vieții reînnoite. Fiți martorii naturii care se deșteaptă din somn sub multe forme, de la mugurii care crapă în deșertul Arizona scăldat de ploi la rățuștele pufoase care sar din cuiburile lor.

programme.title: Urgențe în sălbăticie
programme.desc: Koala Mara are nevoie de o operație de salvare a unui dinte, și o examinați o veveriță rănită cu veterinarul Tim. Agentul de salvare Elise scoate o vulpe zburătoare dintr-un canal și vedeți cum clocesc ouăle de piton ale asistentei Bree.

programme.title: Misterele fluviului Mekong
programme.desc: Nordul temperat întâlnește sudul tropical de-a lungul malurilor Mekongului în Thailanda. Urmează fluviul prin Triunghiul de Aur și vezi dansurile de curtare ale numeroaselor specii de păsări. Apoi, mergi la un festival în onoarea spiritelor apei.

programme.title: Apele Arabiei

programme.title: Secretele pădurilor fermecate
programme.desc: Intrați în ținutul aerului curat și al stâncilor falnice. Urmăriți lupta maimuțelor pentru proviziile de iarnă, cântați alături de lemuri într-un copac plin de fructe și observați un arbore care își unește aroma și oposumii sub clar de lună.

Telemedika
programme.desc: O emisiune care va avea ca invitați medici cunoscuți care ne vor învăța cum să ne ferim de anumite boli, unde vor fi expuse particularitățile acestor boli, dar și discuții despre tipuri de patologii. Emisiunea TeleMedika are un scop educativ pentru a încerca să învețe telespectatorul să prevină apariția diverselor afecțiuni. Formatul permite interacţiunea directă între medicii invitaţi şi telespectatori prin intermediul telefonului şi a reţelelor sociale.

programme.title: Medika special 2
programme.desc: Cu: Dana Chera.

programme.title: Medika special
programme.desc: Cu: Andrada Popovici.

programme.title: Academia de sănătate
programme.desc: Academia de Sănătate este un show informativ bazat, în mare parte, pe interviuri cu renumiți profesori universitari din domeniul medical. Subiectele emisiunii sunt de actualitate şi sunt menite să ridice misterul asupra unor boli cu notorietate și să facă lumină în ceea ce privește actul medical de calitate. Domeniul medical este unul vast din toate punctele de vedere şi de aceea considerăm că introducerea în grila de programe a emisiunilor de acest tip este una benefică pentru telespectatori. În această emisiune telespectatorii au posibilitatea să fie informaţi direct de la cei ce sunt responsabili de actul medical. Formatl show-ului va încuraja dezbaterile, iar finalul va fi uşor de comunicat.

programme.title: Jurnal de viaţă
programme.desc: O emisiune despre excelența în profesia de medic, cu invitați profesioniști în domeniul medical, oameni care performează în acest domeniu. Formatul show-ului este acela de infodoc având linia narativă a unei biografii. Scopul emisiunii este acela de a-i apropia pe campionii domeniului de publicul telespectator, de a prezenta momentele de inflexiune din cariera acestora, performanţele profesionale, planurile de viitor, predincţiile acestora în ceea ce priveşte noile descoperiri şi tendinţe în domeniul lor de expertiză şi activitate.

programme.desc: Tata este epuizat de capriciile fetelor. Medicul său, Laurence, vine cu un plan: să se prefacă bolnav de o boală psihică ce se agravează de fiecare dată când acestea țipă la el. Tata se amuză apoi enervându-și fiicele pe rând, răspunzându-le cu aceeași imaturitate ca ele.

programme.title: Living with Dad 01
programme.desc: Când Tata ratează încă o audiție, fetele îi sugerează să-și găsească o altă slujbă. Nu se așteptau însă ca el să fie copleșit rapid de noile sale responsabilități. Oare n-ar fi mai bine pentru toată lumea dacă ar avea un tată "actor"?

programme.title: Living with Dad 01
programme.desc: Întreaga familie se pregătește cu entuziasm de o binemeritată vacanță la mare. Dar campingul unde făcuse tata rezervarea îi sună pentru a anula din cauza vremii nefavorabile. Au rămas fără vacanță... ... Asta până când Roxane decide să aducă "plaja la ei".

programme.title: Living with Dad 01
programme.desc: Fetele vor să-i ridice moralul tatălui lor și decid să găsească o modalitate de a-l aduce în fața camerei, așa că îl păcălesc să creadă că în apartamentul lor se filmează un reality-show în care familia lor este protagonista. Dar când tata își dă seama că e tras pe sfoară, se hotărăște să le întoarcă farsa fetelor, făcându-le jocul.

programme.title: Living with Dad 01
programme.desc: Petrecerea de ziua lui Ondine e sâmbăta viitoare și ea a planificat totul până în cele mai mici detalii, de la invitați la playlist, la decorațiuni și mâncare. Ziua asta de naștere o să fie PERFECTĂ! Dar când tata îi zâmbește ștrengar, își dă seama că el plănuiește o... surpriză!

programme.desc: In 1964 Opel attacked the upper class. 50 years ago, the Russelsheimer factory brought out the Opel Kapitän, Admiral and Diplomat, short KAD. American style, solid German technology. programme.title: Classic Races
programme.desc: Tropical temperatures, never-ending dust and curves: those are just some of the many difficulties for man and machine during the 1964 Grand Prix in Argentina. This race was responsible for taking the Mercedes brand to the top.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Jaguar is not only the coolest car brand from Britain, but the coolest car brand in the world. While the manufacturer was founded as the Swallow Sidecar Company by Sir William Lyons in 1922, the first Jaguar premiered in 1935. Shortly afterwards the Jaguar SS 100 was introduced, which fascinated with its power, dynamics and elegance and thus paved the ways for models like the XK 120, the E-Type or the XJ. Car History showcases all the models from the SS 100 to the latest F-Type and looks back at Jaguar's success in motorsports.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Jaguar is not only the coolest car brand from Britain, but the coolest car brand in the world. While the manufacturer was founded as the Swallow Sidecar Company by Sir William Lyons in 1922, the first Jaguar premiered in 1935. Shortly afterwards the Jaguar SS 100 was introduced, which fascinated with its power, dynamics and elegance and thus paved the ways for models like the XK 120, the E-Type or the XJ. Car History showcases all the models from the SS 100 to the latest F-Type and looks back at Jaguar's success in motorsports.

An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.

programme.title: Sketchbook
programme.desc: Raphael Federici (street artist), Marine Goodmorning (illustrator), Luca Fiore (cartoonist) and Harry Boudchicha (drawing teacher) reveal their best drawing techniques. Each episode focuses on a specific subject:\r\nmovement, oil painting, shadows, hair... For the first 10 minutes, each artist gives a theoretical lesson illustrated by sketches. Then they each start working on their creation. Finally, they end with a debrief, comparing\r\nand explaining their techniques.

programme.title: Museum Tour
programme.desc: Jean Dubuffet is a theoretician of Raw Art and the most contested and known French artist of the post-war period. In 1969 he decided to build a place for his Cabinet Logologique and at his own expense. This assembly, called La Closerie Falbala, is a pure creation of the mind. This construction site will be considerable, it’s a real artistic and technical challenge. This monumental work is today one of the "youngest" historical monuments in France.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: François Boucq draws from morning to night in his studio, alone, as if he wanted to be more closely involved with his characters, moving from the savagery of the American West to the diplomacy of the Vatican, from the urban jungle to the news of the daily press. He has been drawing for 40 years with realism, with a precise and detailed line, a graphic finesse that makes him one of the undisputed masters of today's comics.

programme.title: Origami
programme.desc: Origami is about the art of paper folding, a Japanese and Chinese millenary tradition. In modern usage, the word “origami” is used as an inclusive term for all paper folding, regardless of their cultural origin. Different folding and sculpting techniques, new models, bright colors – you’ll see all of this in our program! We will teach you how to transform a flat square sheet of paper into a finished sculpture – from simple to complex!

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Between 1883 and 1926 Claude Monet lived in a house at Giverny where he created a flower garden and a water garden, which provided the inspiration for his series of paintings known as the “Water Lilies”. The “Water-Lily Pond” portrays this garden, with its water lilies and the Japanese bridge in the background. In the series of eight large canvases on the theme, housed in the Musée de l’Orangerie in Paris, Monet introduces variations in light according to the hour of the day.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: Artist portrait - Quentin Carnaille
programme.desc: Born 31 years ago in Roubaix, Quentin Carnaille quickly became a force on the art scene north of France. Former architecture student, Carnaille has always been fascinated by how things work. His early works were influenced by clockwork mechanisms, he has diverted from their main use to create jewelry and accessories. It then focuses on the realization of sculptures and greater works with the same aesthetic and inspiration. The contemporary and futuristic ideas influence his work from the beginning, based on its initial orientation on the past and the origins of humanity.

The work that introduces the visit of the exhibition dedicated to this amazing artist is called "silence". The artist represented landscapes of his childhood in the Ardennes in France. But he also painted portraits, paintings representing his mother as his painting entitled "Listening to Schumann".

Savine Faupin, curator of the department Art Brut at LAM, Matthew Morin, connoisseur and collector Christian Berst, owner of the eponymous gallery: each character tries to put his own definition of an art difficult to grasp. Indeed, Raw Art is constantly renewing itself, it is not limited by time or by the style and remains foremost vector emotional message.

He does not define himself as a photographer, but as a creator of installations, the photos being only the representation of his works.

programme.desc: A native of the southern French town of Grasse, Jean-Honoré Fragonard is one of the most important 18th century French painters. He studied at the French Academy in Rome but chose to be free in his work, preferring to carry out private commissions, some of which were licentious, such as “The Shirt Withdrawn” exposed at the Louvre. The “Fanciful Figure” exposed at the Louvre-Lens demonstrates an original and very modern style. One of his masterpieces is without doubt the painting “The Bolt”, in the collection of the Louvre in Paris.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

But she also remains a committed artist. Installed in the popular suburbs of Paris, Annette Messager welcomes us in her workshop.

programme.desc: From “simple” tags to gigantic, colorful murals and collages, street art that was once suppressed is now officially open to the eye of the beholder. When did this shift take place? How do artists themselves experience this change in status and perception? Has their approach evolved along with their art?\r\nTo tell these stories, we've come up with a fabulous playground: Laon's International Urban Arts festival.

programme.desc: In this episode, we meet Cheryl Dunn, photographer. After moving to New York City in the mid-1980s, she spent much of her career photographing the city's streets and the people who made their mark on them. In the late 1990s, she began to focus on film, creating classic films about artists of her generation who influenced the realities of urban life through their own work.

programme.desc: Private Tour takes you to discover the exhibition "The Pushkin Museum: five hundred years of master drawings" at the Fondation Custodia in Paris. The works are displayed in such a way that visitors can observe the evolution of drawings over five centuries. There are drawings by the Italian artist Frederico Zuccari (or Zuccaro) but also the Dutch artist Peter Paul Rubens.

programme.title: Museum stories
programme.desc: In the heart of the Montparnasse district, the Bourdelle Museum remains one of the last testimonies of these groups of artists which flourished in Paris at the threshold of the 20th century. The Antoine Bourdelle Museum offers an opportunity to see the work being created it, as close as possible to the material, in the museum's workshop spirit. Plaster, earth, sandstone and bronzes, but also sketches, variations and variations, reveal the process of development and the working method of an artist as fertile as inventive.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: A key artist of the Italian Renaissance, Raffaello Santi (1483-1520) developed a classical art form, based on drawing, which made him the model for many painters in the following centuries. His favourite theme was the Madonna: you can admire, for example, “The Sistine Madonna” in Dresden and the “The Virgin and Child with St John the Baptist” in the Louvre. Notice the gentle harmony and the delicate sensuality in “The Three Graces” or the powerful human presence in “The Portrait of Baldassare Castiglione”.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: When I grow up I'll be a photographer
programme.desc: In this episode, Christina, a student, is going to play the game and take pictures for a jewelry brand. We will attend a first year image analysis class. The students who did a photoshoot with a duck in the previous episode will edit the photos, and one student will organize a photoshoot on the street.

programme.title: Photo Contest
programme.desc: Two photographers compete on a given theme. Agnès Grégoire, editor-in-chief of PHOTO magazine, will then have to decide between them and choose the best of the two. Today, the Phocaean city is at the heart of the competition: the two competitors must capture the most aesthetic and unusual aspects of it.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: In this episode, we will talk about the artist Antoine Bourdelle. Son of a carpenter who moved to the capital, Antoine Bourdelle became the most important official sculptor at the beginning of the 20th century. This pupil of Rodin took on numerous commissions in France and abroad. But he also kept some of his sculptures still present today in his workshop in the Montparnasse district, a magical place, which has remained frozen in the past.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: In the second half of the 19th century, Edouard Manet (1832-1883) showed great originality in his painting of historic scenes and portraiture of well-known figures, such as the novelist Zola and the poet Mallarmé. Even if we cannot call him the first Impressionist, his leading role in the history of modern art must be emphasised. The scandals in 1863 caused by “The Luncheon on the Grass” or “Olympia” both exposed at the Orsay Museum effectively mark the beginning of modern painting.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: John Singer Sargent - Portraitist of Paradox
programme.desc:
From September 22, 2025 to January 11, 2026, following its presentation at The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the Musée d’Orsay will devote a major exhibition to John Singer Sargent (1856–1925), marking the centenary of the painter’s death.
A century after his passing, John Singer Sargent—celebrated for his portraits of French, English, and American high society during the Belle Époque—remains an enigma. Beneath a façade of carefully maintained respectability, his work nonetheless shocked his contemporaries with its sensuality and candor. Idolized by a wealthy elite eager to pay a fortune to sit for him, another side of his oeuvre reveals his fascination with Bedouins, Spanish dancers, and Venetian gondoliers.
This film offers a portrait full of contradictions: an American born in Florence, we follow him from his nomadic childhood across Europe, through the salons of Paris and London, and finally to the United States, his homeland.
Although immensely successful during his life.

programme.title: The decisive moment
programme.desc: In this episode, we will meet Martin Schoeller, German photographer. His style is characterized by a similar treatment of all subjects photographed, whether they are famous or anonymous. His portraits of Brad Pitt, Steve Carrel, Bradley Cooper and many others, are published in renowned magazines.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: In this episode, we will meet the artist Ben. Active on the contemporary art scene for over 50 years, he is a self-taught, multi-faceted character. His success is undeniable. If his status as an artist is affirmed through his famous writings painted in white cursive letters on a black background, his temperament as a "jack of all trades" has made him one of the most avant-garde artistic personalities in the art world since the 1960s. Attached more than anything else to his region, the artist has been working and living for over 40 years in the heights of Nice, in Saint-Pancrace, in a house where each room can become a studio, and where the progressive lack of space has led him to create an extension, the doors of which he is now opening to us.

programme.title: Warning ! Fresh paint
programme.desc: Move along, there's nothing to see! In April 2018, the Museum "La Piscine de Roubaix" prepared to expand its exhibition space. In a period of six months, several thousand works had to be unhooked, dusted, restored, moved, and reinstalled. These are unique works for which any handling required extreme precautions. Bruno Gaudichon, curator and founder of the museum, had to employ and bring together several workers in ordert to complete a successful reopening.

programme.title: Private Tour
programme.desc: Private Tour takes you to the discovery of the retrospective "Tutto Ponti" which retraces 60 years of the career of the architect-designer Gio Ponti at the decorative arts museum. This is the first retrospective devoted to this Italian artist. You will discover his ceramic works from the beginning of his career, but also the furniture designs anchored in his poetic and subtle universe.

programme.title: We are Artists not Vandals
programme.desc: Born in Le Havre in 1968, CyKlop practices a playful, popular and often interactive art. He is known for his installations of urban furniture that color the city and whose offbeat poetry brings a touch of fantasy to the street. He also uses numerous supports and revisits the myth of Ulysses and the Cyclops through everyday objects that became toys, sculptures or art objects.

programme.desc: In this episode we visit the city of Vallauris where Pablo Picasso became fascinated by the town and the ceramics after visiting an exhibition and it’s where he lived for a decade. The city remains forever marked by the work of this protean artist. Picasso is known in Vallauris for the chapel of the castle and its impressive cycle of paintings entitled "War and Peace". It is also in the museum of ceramics that some of the most beautiful works of the "potter" Picasso are exhibited. The sculpture of “Man with a Sheep”, placed on the Market Square, testifies to the artist's attachment to the city and its inhabitants. In 1959, the castle chapel was inaugurated with his masterpiece "War and Peace" just across the museum Magnelli.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Claude Monet is probably the best-known painter of the impressionist movement. Indeed, the term “impressionism” was derived from his painting “Impression Rising Sun” (1872). This exhibition retraces the great stages in Monet’s prolific career while dwelling on paintings of this master that cannot be ignored: the “Saint Lazare Station”, the “Poppies near Argenteuil”, the “Haystacks” and the “Rouen Cathedral” exposed all around the world in different museum such as the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston without forgetting his “Water-lilies” exposed at the Orangerie museum in Paris. \r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: The decisive moment
programme.desc: In this episode, we'll be talking with Jennifer Khordi, photographer. She is a former computer professional from the Bronx. She started with street photography in the late 1980's and then moved into travel and portrait photography. She has spent the last few years photographing the moon, the Milky Way and New York City.

programme.title: Private Tour
programme.desc: Private Tour takes you to the discovery of the exhibition "Giacometti, between tradition and avant-garde" at the Musée Maillol. This exhibition shows how Giacometti evolved from style to style. It tells his story from the first busts he sculpted at the age of 13, to the realization of large-scale sculptures towards the end of his life.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Although Degas’ art is difficult to classify, it is often associated with the impressionist movement, which emerged in France at the end of the 19th century. Nevertheless, he developed a very personal style with a preference for indoors subjects rather than the open-air scenes favoured by the impressionist painters. The 10 masterpieces presented here are a good illustration of Degas’ preferred themes: the show, the bath, family portraits and the working classes.\r\nDiscover " The Ballet classe " exposed at the Orsay Museum or the " Blue Dancers " at the Fine arts Museum Pouchkine.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Possibly the most renowned painter in the world, Vincent van Gogh was born in Holland in 1853 but spent most of his life in France. Suffering from mental instability, Van Gogh produced more that 2,000 paintings before committing suicide aged 37. You will discover during this visit some of his most famous masterpieces, in particularly two “Self-portraits” at the Orsay Museum, “Sunflowers” exposed at the National Gallery in London, “Starry Night” and the “Church at Auvers-sur-Oise”.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: Othoniel Cosmos - An Artist in Avignon
programme.desc: Cosmos, an Artist in Avignon is a poetic documentary that follows Jean-Michel Othoniel during the creation of his monumental exhibition in Avignon (2025–2026). Through his perspective, the film explores the intimate genesis of his works, from conception to realization, from spirit to matter.\r\nStructured around the four elements, this sensory journey takes us from Jean-Michel’s studio in Montreuil to the workshops of the many artisans collaborating on the project, as well as to the iconic sites of Avignon. The city becomes a stage where the artworks integrate and dialogue with the spaces, between contemporary installation and historical heritage.\r\nThe journey culminates in a choreographic performance by Carolyn Carlson, created for Othoniel’s works and performed by Hugo Marchand and Caroline Osmont, presented for the first time in the courtyard of the Palais des Papes.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: It is in the center of Buenos Aires that Eduardo Stupia decided to install his studio entirely dedicated to creation. In a 20th century house, wedged between two modern buildings, he occupies a large space in which he can indulge in his favorite art, drawing. His works, which he describes himself as abstract landscapes, are drawn with pencil, charcoal or Indian ink. In his heterogeneous compositions, where the graphic language and the precision of the gesture hold a central place, Eduardo Stupia explores the semantics of the drawing and opens the fields of the imagination.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Born in 1866 in Moscow, Wassily Kandinsky is considered as one of the most important 20th century artists. He was notably the founder of abstract art. Having left Russia for Germany where he started teaching at the Bauhaus in 1922, he then settled in France in 1933 and left behind him a particularly abundant work. You will rediscover here his most emblematic creations, essentially drawn from the collection of the Centre Pompidou in Paris.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: Museum stories
programme.desc: The city of Boulogne Billancourt experienced rapid development in the interwar period. Industrialists, filmmakers, architects, painters and sculptors test their creativity there. It is this impetus that the Museum of the 1930s would have liked to transcribe, created a collection of works of art from this period, first constituted by purchases in galleries, flea markets or auction houses, then mainly by donations. More than 1,500 sculptures, 800 paintings, 300 pieces of furniture… A heterogeneous whole, testimony of an era and a place in which the artistic excitement unfolds, and opens the way to a number of creative adventures of the 20th century.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop

Son of a carpenter who moved to the capital, Antoine Bourdelle became the most important official sculptor at the beginning of the 20th century. This pupil of Rodin took on numerous commissions in France and abroad. But he also kept some of his sculptures still present today in his workshop in the Montparnasse district, a magical place, which has remained frozen in the past.

programme.title: Origami
programme.desc: Origami is about the art of paper folding, a Japanese and Chinese millenary tradition. In modern usage, the word “origami” is used as an inclusive term for all paper folding, regardless of their cultural origin. Different folding and sculpting techniques, new models, bright colors – you’ll see all of this in our program! We will teach you how to transform a flat square sheet of paper into a finished sculpture – from simple to complex!

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: In the second half of the 19th century, Edouard Manet (1832-1883) showed great originality in his painting of historic scenes and portraiture of well-known figures, such as the novelist Zola and the poet Mallarmé. Even if we cannot call him the first Impressionist, his leading role in the history of modern art must be emphasised. The scandals in 1863 caused by “The Luncheon on the Grass” or “Olympia” both exposed at the Orsay Museum effectively mark the beginning of modern painting.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: John Singer Sargent - Portraitist of Paradox
programme.desc:
From September 22, 2025 to January 11, 2026, following its presentation at The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the Musée d’Orsay will devote a major exhibition to John Singer Sargent (1856–1925), marking the centenary of the painter’s death.
A century after his passing, John Singer Sargent—celebrated for his portraits of French, English, and American high society during the Belle Époque—remains an enigma. Beneath a façade of carefully maintained respectability, his work nonetheless shocked his contemporaries with its sensuality and candor. Idolized by a wealthy elite eager to pay a fortune to sit for him, another side of his oeuvre reveals his fascination with Bedouins, Spanish dancers, and Venetian gondoliers.
This film offers a portrait full of contradictions: an American born in Florence, we follow him from his nomadic childhood across Europe, through the salons of Paris and London, and finally to the United States, his homeland.
Although immensely successful during his life.

programme.title: The decisive moment
programme.desc: In this episode, we will meet Martin Schoeller, German photographer. His style is characterized by a similar treatment of all subjects photographed, whether they are famous or anonymous. His portraits of Brad Pitt, Steve Carrel, Bradley Cooper and many others, are published in renowned magazines.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: In this episode, we will meet the artist Ben. Active on the contemporary art scene for over 50 years, he is a self-taught, multi-faceted character. His success is undeniable. If his status as an artist is affirmed through his famous writings painted in white cursive letters on a black background, his temperament as a "jack of all trades" has made him one of the most avant-garde artistic personalities in the art world since the 1960s. Attached more than anything else to his region, the artist has been working and living for over 40 years in the heights of Nice, in Saint-Pancrace, in a house where each room can become a studio, and where the progressive lack of space has led him to create an extension, the doors of which he is now opening to us.

programme.title: Graffiti World
programme.desc: Graffiti World is a short program dedicated to contemporary urban art around the world. Each episode explores a specific city, highlighting iconic works of street art. Local soundscape accompanies the images for an authentic, commentary-free immersion. The program showcases the creativity and diversity of artistic expression in public spaces. An invitation to discover the richness of graffiti as an art form in its own right.

programme.title: Warning ! Fresh paint
programme.desc: Move along, there's nothing to see! In April 2018, the Museum "La Piscine de Roubaix" prepared to expand its exhibition space. In a period of six months, several thousand works had to be unhooked, dusted, restored, moved, and reinstalled. These are unique works for which any handling required extreme precautions. Bruno Gaudichon, curator and founder of the museum, had to employ and bring together several workers in ordert to complete a successful reopening.

programme.title: Private Tour
programme.desc: Private Tour takes you to the discovery of the retrospective "Tutto Ponti" which retraces 60 years of the career of the architect-designer Gio Ponti at the decorative arts museum. This is the first retrospective devoted to this Italian artist. You will discover his ceramic works from the beginning of his career, but also the furniture designs anchored in his poetic and subtle universe.

programme.title: We are Artists not Vandals
programme.desc: Born in Le Havre in 1968, CyKlop practices a playful, popular and often interactive art. He is known for his installations of urban furniture that color the city and whose offbeat poetry brings a touch of fantasy to the street. He also uses numerous supports and revisits the myth of Ulysses and the Cyclops through everyday objects that became toys, sculptures or art objects.

The city remains forever marked by the work of this protean artist. Picasso is known in Vallauris for the chapel of the castle and its impressive cycle of paintings entitled "War and Peace". It is also in the museum of ceramics that some of the most beautiful works of the "potter" Picasso are exhibited. The sculpture of “Man with a Sheep”, placed on the Market Square, testifies to the artist's attachment to the city and its inhabitants. In 1959, the castle chapel was inaugurated with his masterpiece "War and Peace" just across the museum Magnelli.

programme.desc: Claude Monet is probably the best-known painter of the impressionist movement. Indeed, the term “impressionism” was derived from his painting “Impression Rising Sun” (1872). This exhibition retraces the great stages in Monet’s prolific career while dwelling on paintings of this master that cannot be ignored: the “Saint Lazare Station”, the “Poppies near Argenteuil”, the “Haystacks” and the “Rouen Cathedral” exposed all around the world in different museum such as the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston without forgetting his “Water-lilies” exposed at the Orangerie museum in Paris. \r\nEnjoy your visit!

She started with street photography in the late 1980's and then moved into travel and portrait photography. She has spent the last few years photographing the moon, the Milky Way and New York City.

programme.title: Private Tour

This exhibition shows how Giacometti evolved from style to style. It tells his story from the first busts he sculpted at the age of 13, to the realization of large-scale sculptures towards the end of his life.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Although Degas’ art is difficult to classify, it is often associated with the impressionist movement, which emerged in France at the end of the 19th century. Nevertheless, he developed a very personal style with a preference for indoors subjects rather than the open-air scenes favoured by the impressionist painters. The 10 masterpieces presented here are a good illustration of Degas’ preferred themes: the show, the bath, family portraits and the working classes.\r\nDiscover " The Ballet classe " exposed at the Orsay Museum or the " Blue Dancers " at the Fine arts Museum Pouchkine.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

You will discover during this visit some of his most famous masterpieces, in particularly two “Self-portraits” at the Orsay Museum, “Sunflowers” exposed at the National Gallery in London, “Starry Night” and the “Church at Auvers-sur-Oise”.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: Othoniel Cosmos - An Artist in Avignon
programme.desc: Cosmos, an Artist in Avignon is a poetic documentary that follows Jean-Michel Othoniel during the creation of his monumental exhibition in Avignon (2025–2026). Through his perspective, the film explores the intimate genesis of his works, from conception to realization, from spirit to matter.\r\nStructured around the four elements, this sensory journey takes us from Jean-Michel’s studio in Montreuil to the workshops of the many artisans collaborating on the project, as well as to the iconic sites of Avignon. The city becomes a stage where the artworks integrate and dialogue with the spaces, between contemporary installation and historical heritage.\r\nThe journey culminates in a choreographic performance by Carolyn Carlson, created for Othoniel’s works and performed by Hugo Marchand and Caroline Osmont, presented for the first time in the courtyard of the Palais des Papes.

programme.title: Artist's Workshop
programme.desc: It is in the center of Buenos Aires that Eduardo Stupia decided to install his studio entirely dedicated to creation. In a 20th century house, wedged between two modern buildings, he occupies a large space in which he can indulge in his favorite art, drawing. His works, which he describes himself as abstract landscapes, are drawn with pencil, charcoal or Indian ink. In his heterogeneous compositions, where the graphic language and the precision of the gesture hold a central place, Eduardo Stupia explores the semantics of the drawing and opens the fields of the imagination.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: Born in 1866 in Moscow, Wassily Kandinsky is considered as one of the most important 20th century artists. He was notably the founder of abstract art. Having left Russia for Germany where he started teaching at the Bauhaus in 1922, he then settled in France in 1933 and left behind him a particularly abundant work. You will rediscover here his most emblematic creations, essentially drawn from the collection of the Centre Pompidou in Paris.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: Museum stories
programme.desc: The city of Boulogne Billancourt experienced rapid development in the interwar period. Industrialists, filmmakers, architects, painters and sculptors test their creativity there. It is this impetus that the Museum of the 1930s would have liked to transcribe, created a collection of works of art from this period, first constituted by purchases in galleries, flea markets or auction houses, then mainly by donations. More than 1,500 sculptures, 800 paintings, 300 pieces of furniture… A heterogeneous whole, testimony of an era and a place in which the artistic excitement unfolds, and opens the way to a number of creative adventures of the 20th century.

This construction site will be considerable, it’s a real artistic and technical challenge. This monumental work is today one of the "youngest" historical monuments in France.

He has been drawing for 40 years with realism, with a precise and detailed line, a graphic finesse that makes him one of the undisputed masters of today's comics.

The “Water-Lily Pond” portrays this garden, with its water lilies and the Japanese bridge in the background. In the series of eight large canvases on the theme, housed in the Musée de l’Orangerie in Paris, Monet introduces variations in light according to the hour of the day.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

The contemporary and futuristic ideas influence his work from the beginning, based on its initial orientation on the past and the origins of humanity.

programme.desc: A key artist of the Italian Renaissance, Raffaello Santi (1483-1520) developed a classical art form, based on drawing, which made him the model for many painters in the following centuries. His favourite theme was the Madonna: you can admire, for example, “The Sistine Madonna” in Dresden and the “The Virgin and Child with St John the Baptist” in the Louvre. Notice the gentle harmony and the delicate sensuality in “The Three Graces” or the powerful human presence in “The Portrait of Baldassare Castiglione”.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

This pupil of Rodin took on numerous commissions in France and abroad. But he also kept some of his sculptures still present today in his workshop in the Montparnasse district, a magical place, which has remained frozen in the past.

programme.title: Within the frame
programme.desc: In the second half of the 19th century, Edouard Manet (1832-1883) showed great originality in his painting of historic scenes and portraiture of well-known figures, such as the novelist Zola and the poet Mallarmé. Even if we cannot call him the first Impressionist, his leading role in the history of modern art must be emphasised. The scandals in 1863 caused by “The Luncheon on the Grass” or “Olympia” both exposed at the Orsay Museum effectively mark the beginning of modern painting.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

programme.title: John Singer Sargent - Portraitist of Paradox
programme.desc:
From September 22, 2025 to January 11, 2026, following its presentation at The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, the Musée d’Orsay will devote a major exhibition to John Singer Sargent (1856–1925), marking the centenary of the painter’s death.
A century after his passing, John Singer Sargent—celebrated for his portraits of French, English, and American high society during the Belle Époque—remains an enigma. Beneath a façade of carefully maintained respectability, his work nonetheless shocked his contemporaries with its sensuality and candor. Idolized by a wealthy elite eager to pay a fortune to sit for him, another side of his oeuvre reveals his fascination with Bedouins, Spanish dancers, and Venetian gondoliers.
This film offers a portrait full of contradictions: an American born in Florence, we follow him from his nomadic childhood across Europe, through the salons of Paris and London, and finally to the United States, his homeland.
Although immensely successful during his life.

programme.desc: In this episode, we will meet the artist Ben. Active on the contemporary art scene for over 50 years, he is a self-taught, multi-faceted character. His success is undeniable. If his status as an artist is affirmed through his famous writings painted in white cursive letters on a black background, his temperament as a "jack of all trades" has made him one of the most avant-garde artistic personalities in the art world since the 1960s. Attached more than anything else to his region, the artist has been working and living for over 40 years in the heights of Nice, in Saint-Pancrace, in a house where each room can become a studio, and where the progressive lack of space has led him to create an extension, the doors of which he is now opening to us.

The sculpture of “Man with a Sheep”, placed on the Market Square, testifies to the artist's attachment to the city and its inhabitants. programme.title: Within the frame

The 10 masterpieces presented here are a good illustration of Degas’ preferred themes: the show, the bath, family portraits and the working classes.\r\nDiscover " The Ballet classe " exposed at the Orsay Museum or the " Blue Dancers " at the Fine arts Museum Pouchkine.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

You will discover during this visit some of his most famous masterpieces, in particularly two “Self-portraits” at the Orsay Museum, “Sunflowers” exposed at the National Gallery in London, “Starry Night” and the “Church at Auvers-sur-Oise”.\r\nEnjoy your visit!

After being ignored for too long, it's time to focus on the artist's early years and the upbringing that enabled him to achieve the extraordinary. Three cities played a key role: Malaga, Barcelona and Paris. Young Picasso traverses them and explores their influence on the artist, analyzing specific works from his early years.
